They create resources offering practical ways you can address violence generally and specifically for transgender survivors and people of color.

Advocates are available 24/7 to talk to anyone who is experiencing domestic violence, looking for information or questioning unhealthy aspects of their relationship. 24 hours a day, seven days a week, 365 days a year, the National Domestic Violence Hotline provides essential tools and support to help survivors of domestic violence so they can live their lives free of abuse. Contacts to The Hotline can expect highly-trained, expert advocates to offer free, confidential, and compassionate support, crisis intervention information, education, and referral services in over 200 languages.

NELA's mission is to empower workers' rights attorneys through legal training, promoting a fair judiciary, and advocating for laws and policies that level the playing field for workers. They aspire to a future in which all workers are treated with dignity and respect; workplaces are equitable, diverse, and inclusive; and the well-being of workers is a priority in business practices. NELA’s continuing legal education programs provide exceptional training and networking opportunities for plaintiffs’ employment lawyers.

The New York Civil Liberties Union (NYCLU) advances civil rights and civil liberties so that all New Yorkers can live with dignity, liberty, justice, and equality. The NYCLU Education Policy Center will advance young people’s civil rights and liberties through legislative advocacy, litigation, community outreach and public education. The Center will focus in the coming years on ending the school-to-prison pipeline, promoting school integration efforts, ensuring safe and supportive schools for all students, and securing comprehensive and inclusive sexuality education across the state. It is the home of the NYCLU’s Teen Activist Project, a youth organizing program that reaches more than 300 young people in New York City.

State watchdog for every jail and prison in New York: county jails, NYC jails, state prisons, youth detention and police lock-ups. People held there, and their family or friends, can file a complaint online about treatment or conditions.

Independent state agency that investigates complaints about the conduct of New York State judges. Complaints must be in writing and signed: file online or by mail to its New York City, Albany or Rochester office.
Takes complaints about insurance companies (including health insurance), banks, student loans, mortgages and other financial services. Weekdays, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

The New York State Department of Health (the Department) has been overseeing the health, safety, and well-being of New Yorkers since 1901 from vaccinations to utilizing new developments in science as critical tools in the prevention and treatment of infectious diseases. In the face of today's new public health challenges and evolving health care system, health equity is foundational to everything they do to help all people achieve optimal physical, mental and social well-being.

They build and support New York’s businesses, helping them find qualified workers and keeping them informed about tools and incentives to make their businesses thrive. They empower and protect New York’s workers by supporting the unemployed and by ensuring all workers have a safe workplace where they receive a fair wage.

Their goal is to empower New Yorkers through various initiatives focusing on civic engagement, leadership development, community service and public safety programs. We Belong Here NY believes that social change can be affected by raising awareness about the prevalence and effects of hate and gender-based violence, bias and discrimination through: education, advocacy, interfaith bridge-building and offering safe spaces and opportunities for youth development, community healing and empowerment.

Wellspring is the domestic violence and sexual assault services resource for Saratoga County and the sexual assault services resource for Washington County. They support survivors by providing emergency shelter, a 24/7 hotline and live chat, counseling, long-term housing assistance, case management and much more. All of their services are free, non-judgmental and confidential. To help spread awareness and promote social change, their advocates work directly with the community through educational and prevention programs.
Wellspring provides services to victims of domestic violence and sexual assault in Saratoga County and they also provide services to victims of sexual assault in Washington County.
Free help for crime victims and their families, friends and loved ones, plus violence prevention education in schools and the community.

Bar association lawyer referral service. Refers you to a local lawyer, including for work problems such as being fired or treated unfairly at work. Ask for a referral with the online form. Ask about the cost of the first meeting.
Takes consumer complaints and wage theft complaints in Westchester County.

County office for public benefits and family services: food benefits (SNAP), cash assistance, Medicaid, heating help (HEAP), child support, protective services for children and adults, and foster care. It also helps with eviction prevention and homeless services.

The District Attorney (DA), also known as a prosecutor, plays a critical role in their criminal justice system. They represent the government in criminal cases and are responsible for ensuring that justice is served by prosecuting individuals accused of committing crimes.
The Victims' Justice Center provides information and referral, criminal justice support, court accompaniment, personal advocacy, counseling and trauma therapy.

The Westchester County Human Rights Commission combats discrimination by implementing and enforcing the County's Human Rights Law and Fair Housing Law and by empowering the community through its education and outreach efforts regarding discrimination and hate-related issues. The Commission accepts, investigates and adjudicates complaints of discrimination in Westchester County in the areas of employment, housing, places of public accommodations, credit lending, and discriminatory harassment.

Help in English and Spanish for victims of domestic violence in Westchester County: safety planning, counseling, advocacy, going with you to court, and help with benefits, compensation, legal services and housing. Offices in White Plains, Yonkers and New Rochelle.

The Westchester Family Justice Center provides confidential and free services to domestic violence, sexual assault and elder abuse victims of crime who access the court to obtain orders of protection in Family Court. Bilingual advocates are on-site in the courthouse to assist clients in navigating the court system, assist with filing for NYS OVS Compensation, court accompaniment, safety planning and information and referrals to other community agencies. Walk-in office hours are Monday- Friday, 9am-5pm (please note: the office is closed daily from 12:30pm-1:30pm)

Free, confidential help for survivors of sexual assault, domestic and partner violence, human trafficking, harassment and stalking: 24-hour bilingual rape crisis hotline, safety planning, going with you to the hospital or court, and help with victim compensation.

Fair housing and housing help in the Lower Hudson Valley: help with housing discrimination, counseling to prevent eviction, foreclosure and utility shut-offs, first-time homebuyer counseling, home changes for aging in place, and independent living for people with mental illness. Most programs are free.

Willow Center’s 24/7 Crisis and Support Hotline is a resource for victims of domestic violence, concerned friends and family, and professionals, 24 hours a day, seven days a week. When you are ready to talk, they are here to listen. Without judgment. Compassionate and trained professionals are available all hours of the day and night – even on holidays – to answer your call.

Help for crime victims across Westchester County: case management, counseling, a 24-hour hotline, information about legal rights, help with medical and social services, transportation, someone to go with you to medical exams and court, safety planning and referrals.

Highly trained helpline advocates can answer general questions about domestic violence, human trafficking, sexual violence, elder abuse and child abuse. They can also give information about their services including residential, community based program and make referrals when appropriate. Helpline advocates can provide crisis counseling and help developing basic safety plan to use if you are not yet ready to seek help. They speak 18+ Asian languages and dialects, and Spanish. All calls are free and confidential.

Womankind provides services to survivors of domestic violence, human trafficking, and sexual violence. Through their programs, they offer a wide variety of services in 18+ Asian languages and dialects, including: a toll-free 24/7 multilingual helpline, safe and confidential emergency housing, culturally-informed counseling, family law and immigration legal assistance, wellness activities, creative arts therapy, support groups, and economic empowerment workshops.

Free, confidential hospital program in Brooklyn for victims of domestic violence, sexual assault or other crime, whatever their gender or immigration status. Rape crisis advocates support victims aged 13 and over in the emergency room on evenings, weekends and holidays.

The Crime Victim/Domestic Violence Program Coordinators assist victims of crime by providing emotional support, case status, victim rights and information about the court process. They arrange meetings between the prosecutor and the victim and request restitution and Orders of Protection. The Program Coordinators also help victims file OVS compensation claims and enroll in the VINE program and parole notification.

Food pantry, food delivery and meals; community gardening; help for crime victims and witnesses; mental health support; hygiene kits; referrals; art programs; and help with medical expenses.

The YWCA of Binghamton and Broome County is dedicated to eliminating racism, empowering women, standing up for social justice, helping families, and strengthening communities, and promoting peace, justice, freedom and dignity for all. YWCA's across the USA serve women and girls in three key areas: Racial Justice and Civil Rights, Empowerment and Economic Advancement, and Health and Safety.

The only licensed domestic violence program in Genesee County: orders of protection, going with you to court, family court petitions, support sessions, safety planning, help finding safe housing and advocacy with other agencies. 24/7 hotline.

YWCA-GCR is committed to advocating for systemic solutions and institutional change for disparities facing women and girls of color. Women come to YWCA-GCR in times of crisis, for safe and affordable housing, help with basic needs, such as food and clothing, victim advocacy, help with addiction, job training and career counseling, and case management.

Free, confidential help for survivors of domestic and sexual violence, whenever the abuse happened and whether or not it was reported: emergency shelter, counseling, support groups, safety planning, someone to go with you for medical, legal and police matters, referrals and victim compensation help.

The YWCA of Niagara Frontier provides services to victims of sexual assault and domestic violence. This agency provides case management services to housing clients, counseling services, emergency safe dwelling, and 24-Hour Hotline Services.

YWCA NENY offers a variety of support services for victims of domestic violence. Services include a 24 hour emergency shelter, counseling, advocacy, financial empowerment services, funding for obtaining housing if homeless due to domestic violence and a 24 hour phone hotline.
Help for women and girls in Rochester and Monroe County facing crises such as homelessness and teen pregnancy, and work for racial justice.
Services in Syracuse and Onondaga County for women and families facing poverty, unsafe housing, unemployment and other hardship, plus youth programs and work against racism.

YWCA of Western New York advocates every day to eliminate racism, empower women, stand up for social justice, help families, and strengthen communities. YWCA WNY has responded to the needs of the community by providing high quality programs and services that promote racial justice and advance women’s empowerment. This commitment continues today through a continuum of comprehensive supports and services, focused specifically on individuals and families living with the inter-related issues associated with poverty and homelessness.
